subject: License sunset and seat rebalance: GitHub, JetBrains, Atlassian renewal windows
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Jade Park <jade@github.com>, Andrey Sokolov <andrey@jetbrains.com>, renewals@atlassian.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: License sunset and seat rebalance: initial ask

Hi all,

We have overlapping renewal windows for GitHub Enterprise (org-wide), JetBrains team licenses, and several Atlassian instances across product and infra teams. Procurement at StarkOps (procurement@starkops.com) asked us to pull together a single plan so we can: 1) reduce overall seat count where usage is thin, 2) align contract end dates where possible, and 3) capture any bundle/volume discounts.

Attached is a quick usage export (starkops_ghe_usage_q1.xlsx) and a compiled license_summary_2027Q2.pdf — the ask is fairly pragmatic: can each vendor provide (by EOD next week) a consolidated renewal quote that includes negotiated multi-product pricing (if applicable), minimum-term vs monthly options, and timing constraints for changing seat counts mid-term?

Key constraints:
- We want to sunset duplicate JetBrains floating seats in Engineering Tools by July 31, 2027 (target).
- GitHub: we have a spike in CI runners — need to understand cost delta if seats drop by 10-15%.
- Atlassian: several small sites could be consolidated under one subscription if pricing is favorable.

Ben/Karthik/Marissa — feel free to add specifics I missed. Jade/Andrey/Atlassian renewals team — please confirm who should be on follow-up calls and what lead times you need for DocuSign windows or PO cutoffs.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of Platform Procurement
Redwood Inference

Attachments: starkops_ghe_usage_q1.xlsx (spreadsheet), license_summary_2027Q2.pdf (summary)

From: Jade Park <jade@github.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: License sunset and seat rebalance: initial ask

Hi Tessa — thanks for the details and the attach. Quick summary from GitHub side:

- We can provide a consolidated Org plan quote. Based on the usage file, a 10% seat reduction would save ~12% annual seat spend but may increase CI runner usage costs depending on runner type.
- We can offer a bundled discount (Org + Advanced Security) if committed for 12 months — approx 8% off list for the combined package.
- DocuSign window: for the quoted pricing to hold, we need a signed agreement within 30 days of the quote date.

I've attached a starter quote stub and a short checklist for running-impact considerations (quote_github_stub.pdf). If helpful, I can set up a 30-minute sync next week with our pricing specialist and your infra lead.

Best,
Jade Park
Strategic Accounts — GitHub

Attachments: quote_github_stub.pdf (PDF), pricing_checklist.txt (text)

On Thu, Mar 30, 2027 at 09:14, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> (original message quoted)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: License sunset and seat rebalance: initial ask

Tessa / team — thanks for pulling this together. A few operational notes from engineering:

- Usage looks skewed: about 40% of JetBrains seats are in very low activity teams (archived projects). Recommend we move those to a smaller shared pool before renewal.
- For GitHub, the main risk with a seat cut is permissions/SCM visibility for a small set of contractors; propose we map those users and convert to a smaller number of paid seats + limited collaborator accounts. That will keep history and PR access but save $$ long term.
- Atlassian: several Confluence spaces are candidates for archival; if we agree to archive by June, we can reduce Confluence user tier by one bucket (per Atlassian tiers) at renewal.

Action items:
1) Procurement to request firm quotes from vendors with explicit seat-change windows and penalties (if any).
2) Marissa to run a final user-mapping pass by Apr 20 to validate targets.
3) Tessa to confirm internal approval cadence so we can sign within vendor DocuSign windows.

If vendors can give us a "flex mid-term" option (e.g., allow a one-time seat reduction inside the first 60 days with pro-rata credit), that's ideal.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Manager, Platform Operations

> On Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 11:06, Jade Park <jade@github.com> wrote:
> > (quoted)

From: Andrey Sokolov <andrey@jetbrains.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 10:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: License sunset and seat rebalance: initial ask

Hi Tessa / Ben / Karthik —

Thanks for the context. JetBrains can support a phased sunsetting approach:
- We can convert floating seats to a shared concurrency pool that reduces the billed seat count by up to 25% provided you consolidate on a single billing instance.
- We need a formal request 45 days before your renewal date to enable the billing adjustment; this is primarily for our procurement and finance systems.

DocuSign: I will issue an amendment with a mid-term reduction clause. The DocuSign link (placeholder) will be live for 21 days from issuance: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/DocuSign-Envelope-XYZ-459

If you want, I can join the call with GitHub next Wednesday to walk through how the concurrency pool works.

Regards,
Andrey Sokolov
Enterprise Accounts — JetBrains

Attachments: jetbrains_concurrency_option.pdf (product brief)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: procurement@starkops.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: License sunset and seat rebalance: authorization to proceed

Procurement — please proceed with consolidated negotiations. Summary of decisions and next steps:

- Approve requesting the GitHub bundled Org + Advanced Security quote (12-month commitment) and push for the 8% bundle discount. Jade has indicated a 30-day sign window.
- Approve JetBrains amendment for concurrency pool with the 45-day notice; Andrey will send DocuSign.
- Atlassian renewals (cc'd earlier) — request a consolidated quote for merging two small Confluence instances into a single instance and provide the price delta.

Marissa — please finalize the user-mapping and confirm which JetBrains seats we will pole off by Apr 20. Ben — once Marissa confirms, please coordinate the internal migration schedule so engineers see minimal disruption.

I'll sign off on the final bundled proposal once procurement brings back the DocuSign envelopes and final PO terms. Attaching a brief approval-slate.pdf for the vendor packet.

Thanks,
Tessa
Head of Platform Procurement
Redwood Inference

Attachments: approval-slate.pdf (PDF)
